references.text: The Lord threatens plague (deber) as punishment for disobedience to the covenant, the same threat found in Deuteronomy 28:21
Jeremiah describes how plague (deber) will strike the people as punishment, in accordance with the curses in Deuteronomy
Ezekiel mentions plague as one of God's four judgments against an unfaithful people, reflecting the covenant curses
David is given a choice between plague and other punishments, and plague is described as the Lord's judgment
Continuation of the same chapter where all the diseases from Egypt are threatened as punishment for disobedience
The Lord could have struck Egypt with plague (deber), demonstrating God's power to wipe out peoples from the earth
The Lord threatens to strike the people of Israel with plague and destroy them, using the same wording as in Deuteronomy 28:21
Amos reminds that the Lord sent plague upon Israel just as He did against Egypt, fulfilling the covenant curses
